\chapter{The model}

\begin{definition}[annotated wiring]\label{def:wiring}
  \defines{n}{integer, $n \ge 1$}\defines{V}{set $\{1,\dots,n\}$}\defines{E}{finite set}\defines{W}{annotated wiring}\defines{s}{map $E\to V$}\defines{t}{map $E\to V$}\defines{\sigma}{map $E\to\{\pm1\}$}\defines{\nu}{map $E\to\{1,2,\dots\}$}
  Fix an integer $n\ge1$ and let $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$. An annotated wiring on $V$ is $W=(E,s,t,\sigma,\nu)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[earlier objects, stub]\label{def:stub}
  \defines{\Omega}{set $(0,\infty)^n$}\defines{\mathcal E}{map $\Omega\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}$}\defines{\eta}{elasticity operator}\defines{H_e}{function $(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$}
  Stub standing for Definitions 1.3--1.10 of the plan.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[matrix unit]\label{def:matrix-unit}
  \uses{def:wiring}
  \defines{M_e}{matrix in $\mathbb R^{n\times n}$}\binds{e,k,l}\defterm{matrix unit}
  For an edge $e$, $M_e\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with $(M_e)_{kl}=1$ if $k=t(e)$ and $l=s(e)$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[the box]\label{lem:box}
  \uses{def:matrix-unit}
  \binds{x,e}
  For every $x\in\Omega$,
  \[ \mathcal E(x)=\sum_{e\in E}\eta[H_e]\bigl(x_{s(e)}\bigr)\,M_e . \]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
  By the definition of $M_e$.
\end{proof}
